bill.title: relative to reporting of civil immigration detentions by state, county, and local law enforcement and correctional facilities.

action.description: Died on Table, Session ended 08/19/2026  HJ 16

posted_text:
👮 NH HB1822 — NH Wants to Know: How Many People Are Held for Immigration Cases

New Hampshire is asking state, county, and local law enforcement – and the facilities where they hold people – to start tracking and reporting how many individuals are detained for civil immigration violations.

Starting December 31, 2026, these agencies will need to submit semi-annual reports to the Attorney General, detailing the number of people detained and the length of their stays.

The Attorney General will then compile this data into a statewide report and share it with the Governor, Senate President, and Speaker of the House.

This reporting requirement is estimated to cost the Department of Justice around $50,505 annually to hire a part-time investigative paralegal to manage the data collection and reporting process.

While the bill itself doesn’t provide funding, it highlights a potential need for staff support to ensure accurate tracking of civil immigration detentions across the state.

Aug. 20, 2026: Died on Table, Session ended 08/19/2026  HJ 16.
